title: Resident Evil: The movie reviews are in
description:
For months gamers and horror movie fans around the world have been waiting for the brand new Resident Evil movie to drop. After the trailer was released there was a huge backlash from fans who were worried that it would be terrible. They said that key characters were missing, it was set in the wrong decade and previous films in the franchise weren’t great. So, now that they’ve seen it, what do they think?

We speak to the film’s director Zach Cregger, BBC reporters Tom Richardson and Baldeep Chahal and six Resident Evil fans to find out about the response to the film and how it compares to the famous game.

Resident Evil audio courtesy of director Zach Creeger and Constantin Film.

Instagram: @bbcwhatintheworld Email: whatintheworld@bbc.co.uk WhatsApp: +44 330 12 33 22 6 Presenter: Iqra Farooq Producers: William Lee Adams, Emma-Louise Amanshia and Mollie Perella Editor: Verity Wilde
summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討全新《Resident Evil》電影上映後的評價與迴響。該片在上映前曾因洩漏的劇本與預告片並未包含遊戲原著角色及劇情，一度引發粉絲強烈質疑。然而上映後，影評人與許多玩家均給予高度好評，認為導演 Zach Cregger 成功將遊玩電玩時的無助與緊張感轉化為電影語言。節目邀請了 BBC 記者 Tom Richardson 與 Baldeep Chahal 以及多位玩家，共同討論電影如何巧妙結合突發驚嚇與幽默感，創下電玩改編電影極高的評價紀錄。
summaryEn: This episode of the BBC podcast What in the World examines the reception and reviews of the new Resident Evil movie directed by Zach Cregger. Before its release, the film faced widespread fan backlash due to a leaked script and trailers showing no original video game characters or direct storylines. However, upon release, both critics and fans praised the film for successfully translating the dread and chaotic tension of playing the games into a cinematic experience, balanced with unexpected humor. Host Iqra Farooq speaks with BBC reporters Tom Richardson and Baldeep Chahal, along with several fans, to discuss how this fresh adaptation became one of the highest-rated video game films to date.
